requirements.title: Mixed numeric intrinsic binary operands are interpreted through result-type conversion with the integer-power exception
requirements.definition: The two operands of a numeric intrinsic binary operation may differ in numeric type or kind type parameter. Except for real or complex raised to an integer power, each operand whose type or kind differs from the result is interpreted as if converted to the result type and kind before the operation is performed. For real or complex raised to an integer power, the integer operand is not required to be converted; that is latitude, not an observable obligation.

requirements.title: Numeric operations express numeric computations and produce numeric values
requirements.definition: A numeric operation expresses a numeric computation and evaluating it produces a numeric value. The permitted operand data types are those specified by 10.1.5.1, not by this subclause independently.

requirements.title: Table 10.3 gives the interpretations of the numeric intrinsic operators
requirements.definition: For a numeric intrinsic expression, Table 10.3 interprets ** as raising x1 to the power x2, / as dividing x1 by x2, * as multiplying x1 by x2, binary - as subtracting x2 from x1, unary - as negating x2, binary + as adding x1 and x2, and unary + as the identity operation on x2. In the table, x1 is the left operand and x2 the right operand. The table extraction was checked row by row; no column ambiguity remains for these rows.

requirements.title: Integer exponentiation with a negative integer exponent is interpreted through reciprocal integer division
requirements.definition: If x1 and x2 are both integer and x2 is negative, x1 ** x2 has the same interpretation as 1/(x1 ** ABS(x2)), subject to the integer division rules of 10.1.5.2.2.
